## Instructions

This quiz provides comprehensive practice across all topics covered this term. Work through each investigation carefully, as this mirrors the exam format. Test your ability to identify designs, select appropriate tests, and interpret results.

---

## Part 1: Conceptual Review

### Question 1: Design Types

Match each scenario to its design type:

Different participants in each condition: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Case study</option></select>

Same participants tested in all conditions: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

Measuring the relationship between two variables without manipulation: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Correlational</option><option value=''>Experimental</option></select>

### Question 2: Test Selection

Two independent groups: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

Same participants, two time points: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value='answer'>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>ANOVA</option></select>

Relationship between two continuous variables: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value='answer'>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

### Question 3: Statistical Significance

p < .05 means the result is: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Definitely true</option><option value='answer'>Statistically significant at alpha = .05</option><option value=''>Practically important</option><option value=''>100% reliable</option></select>

p = .08 means: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Significant at .05</option><option value='answer'>Not significant at .05</option><option value=''>Definitely no effect</option><option value=''>Large effect</option></select>

### Question 4: Effect Sizes

Cohen's d = 0.2 is: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Small</option><option value=''>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Negligible</option></select>

Cohen's d = 0.5 is: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Very large</option></select>

Cohen's d = 0.8 is: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value=''>Medium</option><option value='answer'>Large</option><option value=''>Massive</option></select>

### Question 5: Correlation Interpretation

r = .65 indicates: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Weak positive</option><option value='answer'>Moderate-strong positive</option><option value=''>Weak negative</option><option value=''>Strong negative</option></select>

r = -.40 indicates: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Weak positive</option><option value=''>Strong positive</option><option value='answer'>Moderate negative</option><option value=''>No relationship</option></select>

### Question 6: Key Concepts

Correlation implies causation: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

Effect size tells us practical importance: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

A 95% CI that excludes zero suggests significance at p < .05: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Part 2: Full Investigation Practice

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 1

A researcher tests whether background music affects concentration. 60 participants are randomly assigned to work in silence or with classical music playing. Concentration is measured using an error-counting task.

1. **Design type:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

2. **IV:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Background condition (silence vs music)</option><option value=''>Concentration score</option><option value=''>Number of errors</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

3. **DV:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Music condition</option><option value='answer'>Concentration (error count)</option><option value=''>Participant preference</option><option value=''>Room assignment</option></select>

4. **Appropriate test:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

5. **One-tailed hypothesis:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Music will affect concentration</option><option value='answer'>Participants working in silence will make fewer errors than those with music</option><option value=''>There is no effect of music</option><option value=''>Errors and music are correlated</option></select>

6. **Results: t(58) = 2.34, p = .023, d = 0.61. Significant at alpha = .05?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

7. **Effect size:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Not meaningful</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 2

A researcher measures stress levels before and after a relaxation intervention in 25 participants.

1. **Design type:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Case study</option></select>

2. **IV:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Time (before vs after relaxation)</option><option value=''>Stress level</option><option value=''>Relaxation technique</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

3. **DV:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Time point</option><option value='answer'>Stress level</option><option value=''>Intervention type</option><option value=''>Participant anxiety</option></select>

4. **Appropriate test:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value='answer'>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>ANOVA</option></select>

5. **Results: t(24) = -3.89, p < .001, d = 0.78. The negative t-value indicates:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Error in analysis</option><option value='answer'>Stress decreased (before was higher than after)</option><option value=''>Not significant</option><option value=''>Positive effect</option></select>

6. **Effect size:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium-large</option><option value=''>Very small</option><option value=''>Cannot determine</option></select>

7. **Conclusion:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Stress significantly decreased after relaxation, medium-large effect</option><option value=''>No change in stress</option><option value=''>Stress increased</option><option value=''>Inconclusive</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 3

A researcher examines whether screen time is related to sleep quality in 80 teenagers.

1. **Design type:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Correlational</option><option value=''>Quasi-experimental</option></select>

2. **Is there an IV?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Yes, screen time</option><option value=''>Yes, sleep quality</option><option value='answer'>No IV - both variables are measured</option><option value=''>Yes, age</option></select>

3. **Appropriate test:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value='answer'>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

4. **Results: r(78) = -.42, p < .001. Direction:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Positive</option><option value='answer'>Negative (more screen time, worse sleep)</option><option value=''>No relationship</option><option value=''>Cannot tell</option></select>

5. **Strength:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Weak</option><option value='answer'>Moderate</option><option value=''>Strong</option><option value=''>Perfect</option></select>

6. **Can we conclude screen time CAUSES poor sleep?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

7. **Name a possible third variable:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Stress, depression, or poor time management</option><option value=''>The correlation itself</option><option value=''>Sample size</option><option value=''>p-value</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 4

A researcher compares reaction times between morning people (n=35) and evening people (n=35), tested at 9am.

1. **Design type:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Repeated measures</option></select>

2. **IV:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Chronotype (morning vs evening person)</option><option value=''>Reaction time</option><option value=''>Test time</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

3. **DV:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Chronotype</option><option value='answer'>Reaction time</option><option value=''>Time of testing</option><option value=''>Participant preference</option></select>

4. **Appropriate test:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Correlation</option><option value=''>Regression</option></select>

5. **Results: t(68) = 3.12, p = .003, d = 0.75. Effect size:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium-large</option><option value=''>Negligible</option><option value=''>Cannot interpret</option></select>

6. **Morning people had faster reaction times. Is this causal?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>We can suggest it, but this is quasi-experimental (chronotype not randomly assigned)</option><option value=''>Yes, definitively causal</option><option value=''>No relationship exists</option><option value=''>Cannot interpret without more data</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 5

A regression analysis predicts exam performance from hours of revision:
Performance = 45 + 3.5(Hours), R2 = .38

1. **This analysis allows us to:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Compare groups</option><option value='answer'>Predict performance from revision hours</option><option value=''>Determine causation</option><option value=''>Test for differences</option></select>

2. **The intercept (45) means:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Predicted performance when revision hours = 0</option><option value=''>The slope</option><option value=''>R-squared</option><option value=''>Maximum performance</option></select>

3. **Each additional hour of revision is associated with:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>45 more points</option><option value='answer'>3.5 more points</option><option value=''>38% increase</option><option value=''>No change</option></select>

4. **If someone revises for 10 hours, predicted performance is:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>45</option><option value=''>35</option><option value=''>100</option><option value='answer'>80</option></select>

5. **R2 = .38 means:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>38% of variance in performance is explained by revision</option><option value=''>The correlation is .38</option><option value=''>38% of students improved</option><option value=''>Prediction is 38% accurate</option></select>

6. **The remaining 62% of variance is:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Due to other factors (ability, sleep, test anxiety, etc.)</option><option value=''>Measurement error only</option><option value=''>Proof the model is wrong</option><option value=''>Impossible to explain</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 6

A study reports a 95% CI for the mean difference between two groups: [2.5, 8.3].

1. **Does this CI include zero?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

2. **This suggests the difference is:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Not significant</option><option value='answer'>Statistically significant at p < .05</option><option value=''>Very large</option><option value=''>Zero</option></select>

3. **The point estimate for the difference is approximately:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>2.5</option><option value=''>8.3</option><option value='answer'>5.4 (midpoint of the interval)</option><option value=''>0</option></select>

4. **A narrower CI would indicate:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Larger effect</option><option value='answer'>Greater precision in the estimate</option><option value=''>Non-significance</option><option value=''>Smaller sample</option></select>

5. **If another study found CI [-1.2, 4.8] for the same comparison:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>That result would not be significant (CI includes zero)</option><option value=''>Both studies agree</option><option value=''>The effect is larger</option><option value=''>We should average them</option></select>

:::

---

## Part 3: Quick-Fire Review

### Research Credibility

Pre-registration helps prevent: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Participant dropout</option><option value='answer'>p-hacking and HARKing</option><option value=''>Data collection errors</option><option value=''>Small samples</option></select>

HARKing means: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Honest research</option><option value='answer'>Hypothesising After Results are Known</option><option value=''>High-quality analysis</option><option value=''>Helpful research knowledge</option></select>

Publication bias refers to: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Journals being unfair</option><option value='answer'>Significant results being more likely to be published</option><option value=''>Poor peer review</option><option value=''>Too many publications</option></select>

### Effect Size vs Significance

A result can be significant but have a small effect size: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

A large effect size guarantees statistical significance: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

Effect size is independent of sample size: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

p-value depends partly on sample size: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

### Degrees of Freedom

Independent t-test, n1=20, n2=20: df = <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>40</option><option value='answer'>38</option><option value=''>20</option><option value=''>19</option></select>

Paired t-test, n=30: df = <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>30</option><option value='answer'>29</option><option value=''>28</option><option value=''>60</option></select>

Correlation, n=50: df = <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>50</option><option value=''>49</option><option value='answer'>48</option><option value=''>100</option></select>

---

## Summary Checklist

Before the exam, verify you can:

- [ ] Identify design type from any research description
- [ ] Identify IV and DV (or recognise no IV in correlational designs)
- [ ] Select the appropriate statistical test
- [ ] Write one-tailed and two-tailed hypotheses
- [ ] Interpret p-values correctly
- [ ] Interpret effect sizes (small/medium/large)
- [ ] Interpret confidence intervals
- [ ] Interpret regression output (slope, intercept, R2)
- [ ] Explain why correlation does not imply causation
- [ ] Identify questionable research practices

::: {.callout-important}
## Exam Preparation
Review your previous quiz attempts. Focus on areas where you made errors. Practice identifying designs and tests quickly - this is the foundation for all other questions.
:::
